Malthusian thinking is optimistic; Boserupian thinking is pessimistic

Moving from cropping to hunting and gathering
Leaving land fallow for longer periods

Using mixed materials that cannot be separated

Recycling products at the end of their life

Planning cities to reduce car use

All materials can be recycled forever without loss

questions.q: Which is a common criticism of Malthusian theory?
options: It underestimated technological change in agriculture
It claimed food production grows faster than population
It focused only on energy resources
questions.answer: It underestimated technological change in agriculture
questions.hint: Global food output has grown faster than he predicted.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Evaluate one benefit and one limitation of the circular economy as a strategy for resource stewardship.
questions.hint: Consider waste reduction, costs, consumer behaviour and products that are hard to recycle.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain why some geographers argue that both Malthusian and Boserupian views can be correct in different places or times.
questions.hint: Think about scale, technology, access to capital and environmental limits.

hist-hl.topic: Paper 1 skills: usefulness in context and synthesis of perspectives

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which response best addresses 'value' with reference to purpose?
options: Because the report was written for internal use by the security police, it is valuable as it was less likely to be shaped for public propaganda
The report is valuable because it is long
The report is valuable because it is primary
The purpose of the report was to report things
questions.answer: Because the report was written for internal use by the security police, it is valuable as it was less likely to be shaped for public propaganda
questions.hint: Explain how the purpose affects reliability for a specific inquiry.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why can the same source be both valuable and limited?
options: Its usefulness depends on the question the historian is asking
Only secondary sources can be limited
Value and limitation must always cancel each other out
questions.answer: Its usefulness depends on the question the historian is asking
questions.hint: A propaganda poster is poor on facts but good on methods.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A propaganda poster from a one-party state is most valuable for studying…
options: the methods and messages the regime used to influence people
how many people genuinely supported the regime
questions.answer: the methods and messages the regime used to influence people
questions.hint: Think about what the poster was designed to do.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A memoir written by a former general 20 years after a war is most likely limited because…
options: the author may wish to defend his reputation and memory can fade over time
it was written during the war
questions.answer: the author may wish to defend his reputation and memory can fade over time
questions.hint: Consider both purpose and date.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which phrase best shows awareness of context when assessing a source?
options: Published shortly before an election, the speech may exaggerate the government's successes
The speech was given in a big hall
questions.answer: Published shortly before an election, the speech may exaggerate the government's successes
questions.hint: Context links the timing to the content.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What is the four-letter acronym used for analysing a source's origin, purpose, value and limitations?
questions.hint: Take the first letter of each word.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: How many marks is the final Paper 1 question, which uses sources and own knowledge, worth?
questions.hint: It carries the most marks on the paper.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: At 2.5 minutes per mark, how many minutes should you aim to spend on a 9-mark question? (give a decimal)
questions.hint: Multiply the marks by the minutes per mark.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which is the best way to compare the perspectives of three sources?
options: Identify points of agreement and disagreement, explaining why the perspectives differ
Count which perspective appears most often
Choose the longest source as the most reliable
questions.answer: Identify points of agreement and disagreement, explaining why the perspectives differ
questions.hint: Explain the reasons behind the differences, too.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which sentence shows the best synthesis of sources with own knowledge?
options: Source B's claim that rationing caused unrest is supported by the strikes of the following winter, which Source D does not mention
I know a lot about strikes.
Source D is from a newspaper.
questions.answer: Source B's claim that rationing caused unrest is supported by the strikes of the following winter, which Source D does not mention
questions.hint: Look for sources plus specific own knowledge plus evaluation.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What is a common error in value and limitations answers?
options: Making generic points like 'it is biased' without explaining how this affects the source
questions.answer: Making generic points like 'it is biased' without explaining how this affects the source
questions.hint: Examiners want specific, explained points.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why might two sources from the same date disagree?
options: Their authors had different purposes, audiences and access to information
One of them must be a forgery
Sources from the same date always agree
Historians made a mistake when dating them
questions.answer: Their authors had different purposes, audiences and access to information
questions.hint: Think about origin and purpose.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which is the most useful planning step for the final 9-mark Paper 1 question?
options: Group the sources by the side of the argument they support before writing
questions.answer: Group the sources by the side of the argument they support before writing
questions.hint: Planning makes synthesis easier.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What should the conclusion of a final Paper 1 answer contain?
options: A clear judgement that answers the question, based on the evidence
A new source not in the paper
A list of the sources' authors
A summary of the plot of events with no judgement
questions.answer: A clear judgement that answers the question, based on the evidence
questions.hint: The question usually asks 'to what extent'.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A source is a letter from a fictional factory owner, Mr Ostrov, to a local newspaper in 1931 complaining about new labour laws. With reference to origin, purpose and content, analyse its value and limitations for historians studying reactions to the laws.
questions.hint: Consider who wrote it, to whom, why, and what the content does and does not show.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Using three sources with different perspectives on the causes of an economic crisis, explain how you would build a balanced, synthesized argument under timed conditions. (3–5 sentences)
questions.hint: Mention grouping, contrasting, own knowledge and a final judgement.

hist-sl.topic: Paper 1 skills: usefulness in context and synthesis of perspectives

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In IB History Paper 1, the value and limitations question asks you to refer to which three things?
questions.hint: Think of the OPVL framework.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: How many marks is the value and limitations question (Q2) worth in IB History Paper 1?
questions.hint: It is one of the shorter questions.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: How many marks is IB History Paper 1 worth in total?
questions.hint: Add up the marks of all four questions.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Paper 1 lasts 60 minutes and is worth 24 marks. How many minutes per mark is that? (give a decimal)
questions.hint: Divide the time by the marks.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which is the strongest statement about the value of a source's origin?
options: As a government minister writing in 1936, the author had access to official decisions, so the source is valuable for showing the government's intentions
The source is from 1936, so it is old
The author is a minister, so the source is biased and useless
The source is a speech, so it is valuable
questions.answer: As a government minister writing in 1936, the author had access to official decisions, so the source is valuable for showing the government's intentions
questions.hint: A good point links origin to a specific value for historians.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A private diary written by a soldier during a battle is most likely to be valuable for…
options: understanding the soldier's experience and feelings at the time
knowing the exact number of casualties on both sides
explaining the long-term causes of the war
showing the official policy of the government
questions.answer: understanding the soldier's experience and feelings at the time
questions.hint: Think about what the author could know and why he wrote.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A newspaper cartoon published to criticise a government is most likely limited because…
options: its purpose is to persuade and exaggerate, so it may not present events accurately
it was published at the time
questions.answer: its purpose is to persuade and exaggerate, so it may not present events accurately
questions.hint: Link the limitation to the purpose.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why does context matter when judging a source's usefulness?
options: Events and pressures at the time can shape what the author chose to say or leave out
Context only matters for secondary sources
Context tells you the length of the source
Context makes every source equally reliable
questions.answer: Events and pressures at the time can shape what the author chose to say or leave out
questions.hint: Think about censorship, propaganda or an upcoming election.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A historian's book written 40 years after an event is valuable because…
options: it benefits from hindsight and access to a wider range of evidence
questions.answer: it benefits from hindsight and access to a wider range of evidence
questions.hint: Think about what time allows.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In the OPVL framework, what does the 'P' stand for?
questions.hint: It is about why the source was created.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What does it mean to 'synthesize' sources in an answer?
options: Combine sources thematically with own knowledge to build an argument
Describe each source one after the other
Copy long quotations from each source
Only use the most reliable source
questions.answer: Combine sources thematically with own knowledge to build an argument
questions.hint: Synthesis is about connecting, not listing.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which paragraph opening shows the best synthesis of three sources?
options: Sources A and C both suggest economic hardship drove support for the regime, although Source B emphasises fear of opposition groups.
Source A says that people were poor.
First I will look at Source A, then Source B, then Source C.
All the sources are about the regime.
questions.answer: Sources A and C both suggest economic hardship drove support for the regime, although Source B emphasises fear of opposition groups.
questions.hint: Look for grouping and contrast.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In the final Paper 1 question (9 marks), what must you use?
options: The sources and your own knowledge
questions.answer: The sources and your own knowledge
questions.hint: Both are needed for top marks.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which is the most effective use of time in Paper 1?
options: Spend the most time on the final question, which carries the most marks
Spend equal time on every question
Write the most on the first question
Leave the final question until the last five minutes
questions.answer: Spend the most time on the final question, which carries the most marks
questions.hint: Match time to marks.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A source is a speech by a fictional prime minister, Lord Halvern, given in 1938 to persuade parliament to support a treaty. Analyse one value and one limitation of this source for historians studying the government's foreign policy.
questions.hint: Link the origin and purpose to what the source can and cannot show.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain how you would synthesize three sources that offer different perspectives on why a revolution succeeded, in a timed answer.
questions.hint: Group sources by argument, add own knowledge, and reach a judgement.

math-hl.topic: Rational, exponential and log functions; partial fractions (SL 2.8–2.10, AHL 2.13, 1.11)

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the equation of the vertical asymptote of y = (3x + 1)/(x − 4).
questions.hint: Find where the denominator is zero.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the equation of the horizontal asymptote of y = (3x + 1)/(x − 4).
questions.hint: Compare the leading coefficients.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: When does a rational function have an oblique (slant) asymptote?
options: When the degree of the numerator is exactly one more than the degree of the denominator
When the denominator has a higher degree
When the numerator is a constant
questions.answer: When the degree of the numerator is exactly one more than the degree of the denominator
questions.hint: Think about the result of polynomial division.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the oblique asymptote of y = (x² + 3x + 1)/(x + 1).
questions.hint: Divide x² + 3x + 1 by x + 1 and ignore the remainder.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the oblique asymptote of y = (2x² − x + 3)/(x − 2).
questions.hint: Use polynomial long division.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: State the equation of the horizontal asymptote of y = 2ˣ + 5.
questions.hint: What does 2ˣ approach as x → −∞?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The graph y = ln(x − 3) has a vertical asymptote x = k. Find k.
questions.hint: The argument of ln must be positive.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the x-intercept of y = ln(x + 2).
questions.hint: ln of what number equals 0?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the y-intercept of y = 3e⁻ˣ + 1.
questions.hint: Substitute x = 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The point (8, b) lies on y = log₂x. Find b.
questions.hint: 2 to what power gives 8?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The graphs of y = eˣ and y = ln x are reflections of each other in which line?
questions.hint: They are inverse functions.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find f⁻¹(x) for f(x) = e^(x − 1).
questions.hint: Swap x and y, then take natural logs.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Express (5x + 1)/((x + 1)(x − 1)) in partial fractions.
questions.hint: Use the cover-up method with x = 1 and x = −1.

questions.subject: math
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by (x − 1)(x + 2), then choose a value of x that removes B.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Express 4/(x² − 4) in partial fractions.
questions.hint: Factorise x² − 4 first.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the key features of the graph of y = (x² + 1)/x: asymptotes, intercepts and any turning points. Justify each feature.
questions.hint: Rewrite as x + 1/x, then use the derivative for turning points.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the transformation from y = f(x) to y = f(x) + 3.
questions.hint: A constant added outside f affects y-values.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the transformation from y = f(x) to y = f(x − 2).
questions.hint: Changes inside the bracket do the opposite of what you might expect.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the transformation from y = f(x) to y = f(x + 4).
questions.hint: x + 4 = 0 when x = −4.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the transformation from y = f(x) to y = −f(x).
questions.hint: Every y-value changes sign.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the transformation from y = f(x) to y = f(−x).
questions.hint: Every x-value changes sign.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the transformation from y = f(x) to y = 3f(x).
questions.hint: The multiplier is outside f.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Describe the transformation from y = f(x) to y = f(2x).
questions.hint: Inside the bracket: do the inverse.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The point (2, 5) lies on y = f(x). Write its image on y = f(x) + 1.
questions.hint: Only the y-coordinate changes.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The point (4, −3) lies on y = f(x). Write its image on y = 2f(x).
questions.hint: Multiply the y-coordinate.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The point (6, 1) lies on y = f(x). Write its image on y = f(3x).
questions.hint: Divide the x-coordinate by 3.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The point (1, 4) lies on y = f(x). Write its image on y = f(x − 3).
questions.hint: Move it 3 units right.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The graph of y = x² is translated by the vector (2, −5). What is the new equation?
questions.hint: Horizontal changes go inside the bracket with the opposite sign.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which sequence of transformations maps y = x² to y = 3(x + 1)²?
options: Translation 1 unit left, then vertical stretch scale factor 3
Translation 1 unit right, then vertical stretch scale factor 3
Vertical stretch scale factor 1/3, then translation 1 unit left
Horizontal stretch scale factor 3, then translation 1 unit up
questions.answer: Translation 1 unit left, then vertical stretch scale factor 3
questions.hint: Look at the bracket, then at the multiplier.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The point (3, 4) lies on y = f(x). Write its image on y = 2f(x) + 1.
questions.hint: Stretch first, then translate.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: y = f(x) is translated 2 units down and then reflected in the x-axis. What is the final equation?
questions.hint: Write y = f(x) − 2 first, then make the whole right-hand side negative.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain why y = 2f(x) + 3 and y = 2(f(x) + 3) are different transformations of y = f(x). Use the point (0, 1) on y = f(x) to illustrate.
questions.hint: Expand the second equation and track the point through each order.

phys-hl.topic: B.5 Circuits: internal resistance, emf and potential dividers

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which statement about resistors connected in parallel is correct?
options: They all have the same potential difference across them
They all carry the same current
The total resistance is the sum of the resistances
The total resistance is larger than the largest resistor
questions.answer: They all have the same potential difference across them
questions.hint: Think about which two points every branch is connected between.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Resistors of 3.0 Ω, 5.0 Ω and 7.0 Ω are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: In series, the same current passes through each resistor.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Resistors of 6.0 Ω and 3.0 Ω are connected in parallel. Calculate the total resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: Use 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 12 Ω resistor is connected in series with a pair of 8.0 Ω resistors that are in parallel with each other. Calculate the total resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: Find the parallel part first, then add the series resistor.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which is the best definition of the emf of a cell?
options: The work done per unit charge by the cell in moving charge around the complete circuit
The potential difference across the internal resistance
The force that pushes electrons through the wires
The current per unit resistance in the circuit
questions.answer: The work done per unit charge by the cell in moving charge around the complete circuit
questions.hint: Emf is measured in volts, i.e. joules per coulomb.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 9.0 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω is connected to a 4.0 Ω resistor. Calculate the current in A.
questions.hint: The internal and external resistances are in series: ε = I(R + r).

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 9.0 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω drives a current of 2.0 A through an external resistor. Calculate the terminal potential difference in V.
questions.hint: Subtract the 'lost volts' Ir from the emf.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What informal name is given to the potential difference Ir across the internal resistance of a cell?
questions.hint: It is the part of the emf that does not reach the external circuit.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A battery of emf 6.0 V has a terminal potential difference of 5.6 V when it supplies 0.40 A. Calculate its internal resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: The difference between emf and terminal pd equals Ir.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: For a cell, terminal potential difference V is plotted against current I. The graph is a straight line with gradient −1.5 V A⁻¹. State the internal resistance of the cell in Ω.
questions.hint: Compare the graph with V = ε − Ir.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: On a graph of terminal potential difference V against current I for a cell, what does the y-intercept represent?
questions.hint: What is V when no current flows?

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 12 V supply is connected across a 4.0 kΩ resistor and an 8.0 kΩ resistor in series. Calculate the potential difference across the 8.0 kΩ resistor in V.
questions.hint: The supply pd is shared in the ratio of the resistances.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: An NTC thermistor and a fixed resistor form a potential divider across a constant supply. The temperature rises. What happens to the potential difference across the fixed resistor?
questions.hint: First decide what happens to the thermistor's resistance as it warms up.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A potential divider uses a 6.0 V supply, a 2.0 kΩ fixed resistor and an LDR. In the dark the LDR has a resistance of 10 kΩ. Calculate the potential difference across the LDR in the dark in V.
questions.hint: Use V_out = V_in × R_LDR / (R_LDR + R_fixed).

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 2.0 Ω is connected to an external resistor of 2.0 Ω. Calculate the power dissipated in the external resistor in W.
questions.hint: Find the current first, then use P = I²R.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain why the terminal potential difference of a battery decreases as the current it supplies increases.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to Ir when I gets bigger.

phys-sl.topic: B.5 Circuits: internal resistance, emf and potential dividers

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which statement about resistors connected in series is correct?
options: The same current flows through each resistor
Each resistor has the same potential difference across it
The total resistance is smaller than the smallest resistor
Removing one resistor does not affect the others
questions.answer: The same current flows through each resistor
questions.hint: How many paths can the charge take in a series circuit?

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Resistors of 2.0 Ω, 4.0 Ω and 6.0 Ω are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: In series, resistances simply add.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Two 10 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. Calculate the total resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: Two equal resistors in parallel give a total smaller than either one.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 4.0 Ω resistor and a 12 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. Calculate the total resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: Use 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the SI unit of emf?
questions.hint: Emf is energy transferred per unit charge.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 6.0 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω is connected to a 5.0 Ω resistor. Calculate the current in A.
questions.hint: The total resistance of the circuit is R + r.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 6.0 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω supplies a current of 1.0 A to an external resistor. Calculate the terminal potential difference in V.
questions.hint: Terminal pd = emf − Ir.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 1.5 V has a terminal potential difference of 1.2 V when the current is 0.30 A. Calculate the internal resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: The 'lost volts' equal Ir.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: If the terminals of a cell are joined by a wire of almost zero resistance, what limits the current?
options: The internal resistance of the cell
questions.answer: The internal resistance of the cell
questions.hint: Which resistance is still left in the circuit?

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 9.0 V supply is connected across a 1.0 kΩ resistor and a 2.0 kΩ resistor in series. Calculate the potential difference across the 2.0 kΩ resistor in V.
questions.hint: The larger resistor takes the larger share of the pd.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 10 V supply is connected across a 1.0 kΩ resistor in series with a resistor R. The potential difference across the 1.0 kΩ resistor is 2.5 V. Calculate R in kΩ.
questions.hint: Find the pd across R first, then use the fact that the current is the same in both.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR) as the light intensity increases?
questions.hint: LDRs are used in circuits that turn street lights on at night.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Name the component whose resistance decreases as its temperature increases (NTC type).
questions.hint: Its name combines 'thermal' and 'resistor'.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: An LDR and a fixed resistor form a potential divider across a constant supply. It gets darker. What happens to the potential difference across the fixed resistor?
questions.hint: First decide whether the LDR's resistance goes up or down in the dark.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 4.5 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω is connected to a 4.0 Ω resistor. Calculate the power dissipated in the 4.0 Ω resistor in W.
questions.hint: Find the current first, then use P = I²R.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain how a potential divider containing a thermistor could be used to switch on a heater when a room gets cold.
questions.hint: Describe how the thermistor's resistance and the output voltage change as the temperature falls.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which is the best description of a flashbulb memory?
options: A vivid, detailed memory of the circumstances in which a person learned of a surprising, emotional event
A memory of a photograph seen in the news
A memory that is lost immediately after an emotional event
A procedural memory for a well-practised skill
questions.answer: A vivid, detailed memory of the circumstances in which a person learned of a surprising, emotional event
questions.hint: Focus on the circumstances of hearing the news, not the event itself.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which almond-shaped brain structure is most associated with processing emotion and enhancing the memory of emotional events?
questions.hint: It is part of the limbic system, close to the hippocampus.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: The original theory of flashbulb memory proposed that these memories are formed by:
options: A special neural mechanism triggered by high surprise and personal consequence
Repeated rehearsal alone, with no role for emotion
The same processes as any trivial everyday memory
questions.answer: A special neural mechanism triggered by high surprise and personal consequence
questions.hint: The theory suggested the brain 'takes a picture' at a critical moment.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which of these is one of the typical features people recall in a flashbulb memory?
options: Where they were when they heard the news
The exact date of the event's anniversary
The names of all the people involved in the event
The weather forecast for the following week
questions.answer: Where they were when they heard the news
questions.hint: Think about the personal context of receiving the news.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which research design is most commonly used to study flashbulb memories after a major public event?
options: Test–retest questionnaires comparing a person's accounts over time
Laboratory experiments that create a national tragedy
Case studies of a single brain-damaged patient
Twin studies comparing identical and fraternal twins
questions.answer: Test–retest questionnaires comparing a person's accounts over time
questions.hint: Researchers cannot create the event, so they survey people after it happens.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Longitudinal studies of memories of a space shuttle disaster found that, years later:
options: Many accounts had changed considerably, yet confidence remained high
Accounts were almost perfectly identical to the first reports
Participants could no longer remember the event at all
Confidence fell in line with accuracy
questions.answer: Many accounts had changed considerably, yet confidence remained high
questions.hint: Compare what changed (the details) with what did not (how sure people felt).

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A study comparing memories of a major terrorist attack with memories of an everyday event from the same time found that:
options: Both declined in consistency at similar rates, but vividness and confidence stayed higher for the emotional memory
The emotional memory stayed perfectly consistent while the everyday memory faded
Both memories were forgotten completely within a month
The everyday memory was rated as more vivid
questions.answer: Both declined in consistency at similar rates, but vividness and confidence stayed higher for the emotional memory
questions.hint: The key difference was in how the memories felt, not how accurate they were.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Why do flashbulb memory researchers often use consistency between accounts as a measure of accuracy?
options: Because what each participant was actually doing can rarely be verified independently
Because consistency is always identical to accuracy
Because participants refuse to answer questions about accuracy
Because brain scans cannot be used in psychology
questions.answer: Because what each participant was actually doing can rarely be verified independently
questions.hint: Who could check where each person really was when they heard the news?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What term describes the extent to which a measure gives the same results when it is repeated?
questions.hint: This is different from validity.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A brain-imaging study found that participants who had been physically closer to a major attack showed what when recalling it?
options: Less hippocampal activity than when recalling everyday events of any kind
Activation only in the visual cortex
questions.hint: Closer to the event usually means more emotional arousal.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which best describes the relationship between confidence and accuracy in flashbulb memory research?
options: Confidence often remains high even when accuracy declines
Confidence and accuracy always rise together
Accuracy increases over time while confidence falls
questions.answer: Confidence often remains high even when accuracy declines
questions.hint: Feeling certain is not the same as being correct.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which hormone, released during emotional arousal, is thought to strengthen memory consolidation through its effects on the amygdala?
questions.hint: It is part of the 'fight or flight' response.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Why is it difficult to establish causation in flashbulb memory research?
options: The event cannot be manipulated, so variables such as rehearsal and media exposure are uncontrolled
Researchers are not allowed to ask about memories
questions.answer: The event cannot be manipulated, so variables such as rehearsal and media exposure are uncontrolled
questions.hint: Think about what a true experiment needs that these studies lack.

questions.subject: psych

Walking the same route to school every day

It stores all long-term memories by itself

It reduces the strength of emotional memories

How emotional a person feels when remembering

questions.hint: Researchers compare a later account with an earlier one.

questions.q: Why do researchers usually test participants soon after the event and again months later?

To make participants forget the event
To find out which participants are lying

Emotion has no effect on memory

Never thinking about the event again

Having no emotional reaction to the event

questions.subject: psych

People are never confident about memories

questions.hint: Compare vividness and confidence with consistency over time.

tok.topic: Mathematics: discovered or invented? Applications and beauty

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Which view holds that mathematical objects exist independently of human minds?
questions.hint: Think of a realm of perfect abstract forms.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: According to formalism, mathematics is best described as…
options: the manipulation of symbols according to agreed rules
the discovery of objects in an abstract realm
questions.answer: the manipulation of symbols according to agreed rules
questions.hint: Focus on symbols and rules rather than meaning.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: In TOK, what is the name for a statement accepted without proof as a starting point for a mathematical system?
questions.hint: Every proof has to start somewhere.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Which observation is most often used to support the claim that mathematics is discovered?
options: Mathematicians working separately often reach the same results
Different cultures use different symbols for numbers
questions.answer: Mathematicians working separately often reach the same results
questions.hint: If it were purely invented, would independent work converge?

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Which observation best supports the claim that mathematics is invented?
options: Changing the starting axioms produces different but consistent geometries
Prime numbers appear in many contexts
Calculations give the same answer every time
questions.answer: Changing the starting axioms produces different but consistent geometries
questions.hint: Who chooses the starting points?

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Non-Euclidean geometries were developed by replacing which of Euclid's postulates?
questions.hint: It concerns lines that never meet.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: The phrase 'the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics' refers to…
options: abstract mathematics turning out to describe the physical world very well
mathematics being too hard for most people
questions.answer: abstract mathematics turning out to describe the physical world very well
questions.hint: Consider why ideas developed on paper fit nature.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Which is an example of 'pure' mathematics later finding a major practical application?
options: Number theory about prime numbers used in online encryption
questions.answer: Number theory about prime numbers used in online encryption
questions.hint: Look for an area once studied only for its own sake.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: In mathematics, 'abstraction' means…
options: removing specific details to focus on general structure
adding real-world examples to a proof
guessing an answer from a diagram
questions.answer: removing specific details to focus on general structure
questions.hint: What happens when 3 apples become just '3'?

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Mathematicians often call a proof 'elegant' when it…
options: is short, clear and reveals why the result is true
uses as many steps as possible
is written in a foreign language
questions.answer: is short, clear and reveals why the result is true
questions.hint: Think of economy and insight.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Which proof technique assumes the opposite of what is to be proved and shows this leads to an impossibility?
questions.hint: The assumption 'breaks' the system.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Which is the best-formed TOK knowledge question?
options: To what extent is mathematical knowledge discovered rather than created?
What is the formula for the area of a circle?
questions.answer: To what extent is mathematical knowledge discovered rather than created?
questions.hint: Knowledge questions are open, contestable and about knowledge itself.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: A formalist might respond to the question 'Does the number 7 exist?' by saying…
options: it exists only as a symbol within a system of rules
it exists in a perfect abstract realm
it exists as seven physical objects
questions.answer: it exists only as a symbol within a system of rules
questions.hint: Recall what formalism focuses on.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: Explain how the success of mathematics in describing the physical world could be used to support the claim that mathematics is discovered. Include one counterclaim.
questions.hint: Ask why invented rules would match nature so closely, then consider whether we select the mathematics that fits.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: To what extent should beauty or elegance be used to judge the value of mathematical knowledge?
questions.hint: Consider whether elegant proofs are more often true, more useful or simply more satisfying.

questions.subject: tok
questions.q: 'Mathematics is a language that humans created.' Discuss this claim with reference to at least one example.
questions.hint: Compare the symbols we choose with the relationships they express.
